name: Deering Estate's Champion Black Olive

location.address: Charles Deering Estate, 16701 SW 72nd Ave, Palmetto Bay, FL 33157 (beside the Stone House)

official_register.name: Florida Forest Service Champion Tree Register (National Champion, OBJECTID 223)

access: Paid entry to the Deering Estate grounds (about $15 to $18 for adults per search pointers; hours not confirmed on a fetched official page, deeringestate.org returns 403 or a JS shell). Check hours before going. The Stone House itself was reported closed for restoration from 2025-04-28 but the tree stands outside it.
verify_notes: ONE SOURCE PLUS A 2026 OBSERVATION, flagged. Register (official, fetched via Wayback snapshot 2023-05-02 in an earlier pass): National Champion Bucida buceras, 158 in = 401 cm circumference, 64 ft = 19.5 m, crown 83 x 59 ft, measured 2020-01, register coordinate 25.61593,-80.30663 (beside the Stone House, built 1922 by Charles Deering). UF/IFAS Extension Miami-Dade blog dated 2026-09-11 (fetched this pass) shows a Florida Forest Service forester and Deering Estate's conservation specialist visiting a black olive at Deering Estate 'next to a building' with 'an old cavity in its trunk' and measuring 182 in circumference, 70 ft, crown 81 ft, 272 points; the author calls it the biggest black olive in Florida and maybe in the continental USA. This is evidence the champion is alive in 2026. CONFLICT: girth 182 in (2026) vs 158 in (2020 register); a 24 in rise in six years is implausible for growth, so either remeasurement differences (cavity, buttress height) or a different tree. Not proven to be the same tree; the writer must say 'register' and 'extension blog' figures separately and not merge them. Girth_cm and height_m here use the register values only. Age: no source; Stone House dates 1922, but no source ties this tree to that planting, so no age. Pin is the register point, approximate (no tree-level evidence). Not rich; tree is paid entry. Nearby, same estate, still leads: Florida Strangler Fig (OBJECTID 439, 25.62356,-80.30434) and Gumbo-limbo (OBJECTID 694, 25.618,-80.30654). Hosts: deeringestate.org 403/JS shell (two attempts, Wayback plan-your-visit snapshot is an empty shell); ffs.fdacs.gov refuses connections, Wayback only.
story:
The biggest black olive in the United States, by the state register, grows beside Charles Deering's Stone House in Palmetto Bay. The Florida Forest Service lists it as the National Champion of its species, measured in January 2020 at 19.5 metres tall, with a trunk 401 centimetres round and a crown about 25 by 18 metres.

Then came a second measurement, and it does not agree. In September 2026 the University of Florida's extension office in Miami-Dade published an account of a state forester and the estate's conservation specialist measuring a black olive at Deering Estate, next to a building, with an old cavity in its trunk. They found 182 inches round, about 4.6 metres, and 70 feet tall, and the author called it the biggest black olive in Florida and perhaps the continental US. That is 60 centimetres more trunk than the register found six years earlier, too much for growth alone. Either the tape went round a different height of a hollowed trunk, or it is another tree. Nobody has said which.

The Stone House went up in 1922. No source ties the tree to that year, so it has no age on our page. If you know when it was planted, tell us.

Entry to the Deering Estate grounds is paid, so check opening hours before you go. The Stone House was reported closed for restoration from April 2025, but the tree stands outside it. Our pin is the register's point, not a fix on the trunk.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by a trunk about four metres round, with an old cavity in it if this is the tree the 2026 measurers saw. It stands beside the Stone House on the Deering Estate.
